questions.prompt: During physiologic calibrations, the patient performs right leg movement but the right anterior tibialis channel remains flat while the video confirms movement. What is the best first response?
options: Increase the high-frequency filter to make the signal appear
Begin the study and document the flat channel in the morning
Check the electrode/sensor connection and correct the channel before lights out
Tell the patient to move both legs continuously
questions.answer: Check the electrode/sensor connection and correct the channel before lights out
questions.rationale: Physiologic calibration is the first test of patient-signal integrity; unexpected absent response should be corrected before starting.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is accepting a bad baseline because the patient is ready for sleep.
questions.coachBobNote: Physiocals are your preflight check. Do not take off with a dead engine.

questions.prompt: Two EEG electrodes have very different impedances and the channel shows prominent 60-Hz artifact. Which principle explains why equal electrode quality matters?
options: Common mode rejection works best when input impedances are low and relatively balanced
High impedance improves common mode rejection
A notch filter permanently repairs electrode contact
Ground electrodes record sleep spindles
questions.answer: Common mode rejection works best when input impedances are low and relatively balanced
questions.rationale: Differential amplifiers reject common noise best when electrode impedances are low and balanced.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is thinking the filter should fix a skin-prep problem.
questions.coachBobNote: Fix the source before you polish the noise.

questions.prompt: Modern digital PSG systems commonly store individual electrode data against a system reference. Why is that useful?
options: It removes the need for electrode placement accuracy
It allows reformatting/remontaging during review if the recording supports it
It prevents all artifact from occurring
It means physician orders are unnecessary
questions.answer: It allows reformatting/remontaging during review if the recording supports it
questions.rationale: Digital systems often allow derived montages from stored referenced signals, but only if original signals and placements are valid.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is thinking remontaging can rescue bad setup.
questions.coachBobNote: Reformatting helps only if you collected good ingredients.

questions.prompt: A nasal pressure channel abruptly becomes flat after the patient turns, but thoracoabdominal effort and video suggest continued breathing. What is the best first action?
options: Check the cannula/sensor position and tubing for displacement or blockage
Ignore the channel because respiratory belts are enough for all scoring
Increase CPAP pressure if this is diagnostic PSG
Score central apnea immediately
questions.answer: Check the cannula/sensor position and tubing for displacement or blockage
questions.rationale: Sensor displacement or blockage can mimic absent airflow; troubleshoot before scoring a physiologic event.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is scoring artifact as apnea.
questions.coachBobNote: Trust patterns, not one lonely channel.

questions.prompt: A patient complains of tingling when touching equipment during setup. What is the best response?
options: Tell the patient tingling is normal with EEG electrodes
Continue because PSG currents are always harmless
Stop and assess electrical safety according to facility protocol before continuing
Add a second ground wire to the patient without checking equipment
questions.answer: Stop and assess electrical safety according to facility protocol before continuing
questions.rationale: Electrical-safety complaints must be assessed and escalated per policy; patient safety comes first.
questions.whyTricky: The trap is minimizing patient-reported symptoms during a technical setup.
questions.coachBobNote: When a patient says shock, you stop and check.
